blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ اَنَّ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَ: لَيْسَ الشَّدِيْدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ، اِنَّمَا الشَّدِيْدُ الَّذِيْ يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه البخاري باب الحذر من الغضب رقم:٦١١٤
blocks.tamil_translation: The strong one is not the one who throws down (his opponent). Rather, the strong one is the one who controls himself when anger comes” — Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said this.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ ذَرٍّ ﵁ قَالَ: اِنَّ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَ لَنَا: اِذَا غَضِبَ اَحَدُكُمْ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ فَلْيَجْلِسْ، فَاِنْ ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ الْغَضَبُ وَاِلَّا فَلْيَضْطَجِعْ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابوداؤد باب مايقال عند الغضب رقم:٤٧٨٢
blocks.tamil_translation: “When any one of you becomes angry, if he is standing let him sit down; if the anger goes away, well and good; otherwise let him lie down” — Hazrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said this.

blocks.text:
Explanation:- The meaning of the hadith is that, so that the consequence of anger may be as little as possible, one should change to whichever posture brings calm to the heart. There is a chance of less harm occurring by sitting than by standing, and by lying down than by sitting.
(Mazahir-e-Haq)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ﵄ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ اَنَّهُ قَالَ: عَلِّمُوْا وَبَشِّرُوْا وَلَا تُعَسِّرُوْا، وَاِذَا غَضِبَ اَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَسْكُتْ.
blocks.tamil_translation: “Teach people the Deen, give good news, do not create difficulties, and if any of you becomes angry, let him become silent” — Hazrat Ibn Abbas (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said this.
